import os
import subprocess
import sys

from sase.vcs_provider import get_vcs_provider

checkout_target = {{ setup.checkout_target | tojson }}
project_name = {{ setup.project_name | tojson }}
gh_ref = {{ gh_ref | tojson }}

provider = get_vcs_provider(os.getcwd())

# Checkout the PR branch so that subsequent diffs are relative to the
# PR tip rather than the default branch. Try checkout_target first
# (works for default-branch refs like origin/main), then fall back to
# Patch name -> branch name conversion.
is_patch = checkout_target == f"origin/{gh_ref}"
ok, err = provider.checkout(checkout_target, os.getcwd())
if not ok:
    if is_patch:
        # Patch ref — resolve name to branch name
        resolved = provider.resolve_revision(
            gh_ref, project_name, os.getcwd()
        )
        ok, err = provider.checkout(resolved, os.getcwd())
    else:
        # Project/repo ref — try common default branch names
        for fallback in ["master", "main"]:
            ok, err = provider.checkout(fallback, os.getcwd())
            if ok:
                break
    if not ok:
        print(
            f"Warning: checkout failed: {err}",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )

# Sync with remote after checkout
subprocess.run(
    ["git", "pull", "--rebase", "--quiet"],
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
    check=False,
)

# Record HEAD for the diff step
result = subprocess.run(
    ["git", "rev-parse", "HEAD"],
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
    check=False,
)
head = result.stdout.strip() if result.returncode == 0 else ""
print(f"head_before={head}")
print("success=true")

head_before="{{ checkout.head_before }}"
if [ -z "$head_before" ]; then
  exit 0
fi
head_now=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
diff_dir="${SASE_TMPDIR:-${SASE_HOME:-$HOME/.sase}/tmp}/gh-diffs"
mkdir -p "$diff_dir"
diff_file=$(mktemp "$diff_dir/sase-gh-XXXXXX.diff")
if [ "$head_now" != "$head_before" ]; then
  # Commits were made — show only the last commit's diff
  git diff HEAD~1 HEAD > "$diff_file" 2>/dev/null
  commit_msg=$(git log -1 --format='%s' HEAD)
  echo "meta_commit_message=$commit_msg"
else
  # No commits — show uncommitted changes
  git diff HEAD > "$diff_file" 2>/dev/null
  git ls-files --others --exclude-standard -z 2>/dev/null \
    | while IFS= read -r -d '' f; do
        git diff --no-index /dev/null "$f" 2>/dev/null
      done >> "$diff_file"
fi
if [ -s "$diff_file" ]; then
  echo "diff_path=$diff_file"
else
  rm -f "$diff_file"
fi

# Stash any uncommitted changes (including untracked files)
if ! git diff --quiet HEAD 2>/dev/null || [ -n "$(git ls-files --others --exclude-standard)" ]; then
  git stash push --include-untracked -m "gh-workflow-$(date +%s)" --quiet
  echo "stashed=true"
else
  echo "stashed=false"
fi
git fetch origin --quiet 2>&1 || true
git pull --rebase --quiet 2>/dev/null || true
echo "success=true"

from sase_github.scripts.gh_setup import main
main(
    gh_ref={{ gh_ref | tojson }},
    n={{ n | tojson }},
    release={{ release | tojson }},
    workflow_label={{ workflow_label | tojson }},
)

**Read next, in this order:**

1. **Hutchins, *How a Cockpit Remembers Its Speeds* (1995)** — [PDF](https://www.ida.liu.se/~729G12/mtrl/cockpit.pdf). The system remembers; the TUI is putting instruments back.
2. **Bainbridge, *Ironies of Automation* (1983)** — [PDF](https://gwern.net/doc/sociology/technology/1983-bainbridge.pdf). Why “watch every agent” is the wrong leftover human task.
3. **Naur, *Programming as Theory Building* (1985)** — [PDF](https://pages.cs.wisc.edu/~remzi/Naur.pdf). Understanding stays human; text is a deposit, not a substitute.
4. **LongHorizon-Harness (arXiv:2608.01964)** — task state outside execution; wrap native loops; Manage–Execute–Audit with a fresh-context executor.
5. **Willison, *Embracing the parallel coding agent lifestyle*** plus *An LLM agent runs tools in a loop to achieve a goal* — the window farm, named, with the noun **goal**.
6. **Temporal, *Durable, flexible multi-agent systems* (2026)** — the layer under the framework; a human wait is durable state.
7. **Karpathy, Software 3.0** ([Latent Space](https://www.latent.space/p/s3)) — autonomy slider, verifiability, you cannot outsource understanding.
8. ***When Sub-Agents Work in Parallel* (arXiv:2610.10263)** — orchestration dominates on long-horizon work; 13 concurrency failure modes.
9. **Cursor, *Continually improving our agent harness*** — inner-loop competitor; decline to become a second Cursor.
10. **Parasuraman, Sheridan, Wickens (2000)** — typed levels of automation; vocabulary for `%auto`.
11. **Endsley, situation awareness (1995)** — goal-directed displays; unread-done as SA2/SA3.
12. **METR long-task horizon (arXiv:2503.14499)** — why the operating layer is timely.

Book analog if the papers are not enough metaphor: Marquet, *Turn the Ship Around!* (intent-based leadership).
